brokers.note: A copy of Apache RocketMQ coded for its HTTP interface, which delivers FirstConsumeTime and NextConsumeTime, fields Apache RocketMQ lacks. Its TCP interface and the 5.x series speak RocketMQ's own protocols and are answered by the Apache RocketMQ record.

read_back.question: Q3

You must acknowledge all messages in a batch before the broker delivers the next batch from the same partition.
A single call may return messages from multiple partitions.
This interface is suitable for globally order and partitionally order messages, and could be used in multi-thread scenes.
Long polling ( waitseconds > 0) The broker holds the request open until a message arrives or the timeout elapses.

Q7.note: Judgment: several long-polling requests can wait at once (the SDK allows several threads), and a response can carry several partitions' messages; within a partition the next batch goes out only after every message of the current one is acknowledged, so the acknowledgment acts as a credit of one batch per partition, as RabbitMQ's prefetch was coded.
